items.raw_snippet: # SpaceX pursues confidential IPO in March following xAI merger, aiming for a $1.75T valuation. SpaceX planning confidential IPO filing, eyeing a June listing and up to $1.75T–$2T valuation after xAI deal. Elon Musk’s space exploration giant, SpaceX, is reportedly preparing to take the next step toward going public with one of the most anticipated IPOs in history. Following its recent merger with Musk's artificial intelligence startup, xAI, the company is said to be targeting a staggering $1.75 trillion valuation. According to reports from Bloomberg, SpaceX plans to submit draft paperwork to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in March under a confidential filing. At its projected $1.75 trillion valuation, the SpaceX offering would far surpass Saudi Aramco’s $29 billion debut in 2019, which currently holds the record for the largest IPO in history. The company's proposed valuation follows its recent acquisition of xAI, Musk’s artificial intelligence venture. With its bold ambitions and the momentum from its xAI merger, SpaceX is poised to make history.

items.raw_snippet: # Is Elon Musk trying to influence SpaceX’s valuation ahead of IPO. It looks like Elon Musk is trying to make it seem that SpaceX is more valuable than it actually is. Musk’s rocket company SpaceX has acquired xAI, the artificial intelligence firm founded by himself three years ago, in a massive, and unconventional, deal that combines the two privately held firms into a company with an astounding $1.25 trillion reported valuation and plans for a historic IPO this year. The deal, described as unconventional due to both companies being privately held and founded by the same individual, signals Musk’s ambition to integrate his ventures in aerospace and artificial intelligence under one corporate umbrella. Analysts note that the consolidation could streamline operations, accelerate research, and allow Musk to leverage cross-disciplinary technologies, from AI‑driven space exploration systems to autonomous robotics and computational simulations for aerospace applications. **READ: Elon Musk reignites row over LinkedIn’s Hoffman’s Trump ‘martyr’ remark (**. While the precise terms of the acquisition have not been publicly disclosed, the strategic implications are significant: it aligns Musk’s AI initiatives with SpaceX’s long-term space ambitions, potentially creating synergies between AI software development and spacecraft engineering. Beyond the technical and financial aspects, the merger carries symbolic weight, highlighting Musk’s continued influence over two of the most transformative industries of the 21st century. By uniting xAI with SpaceX, Musk supposedly reinforces a vision of integrated technological ecosystems, in which AI and space exploration support and amplify each other. Musk cited the potential for space-based data centers, the energy-intensive computing facilities necessary to power AI services, as one of the most important benefits of the combination, even though the concept is still unproven and largely theoretical. For Elon Musk, the merger of SpaceX and xAI represents more than just a business transaction, it is a strategic statement about his vision for the future of technology. **READ: Elon Musk explores company merger as SpaceX IPO nears (**. By bringing his aerospace and AI ventures together, Musk positions himself at the intersection of two of the most transformative industries of the 21st century, signaling his intent to shape the direction of both sectors simultaneously. # SpaceX xAI Merger Valued at $1.25 Trillion Ahead of Mega IPO. SpaceX is set to merge with xAI, the artificial intelligence startup founded by Elon Musk, in a deal that would value the combined entity at about $1.25 trillion, according to media reports citing people familiar with the matter. The proposed merger would combine SpaceX’s space launch and satellite internet operations with xAI’s artificial intelligence research, creating a single company spanning aerospace, communications and AI development. ## Merger Brings Together Space and AI Businesses. Under the plan, SpaceX will absorb xAI, aligning the AI firm more closely with Musk’s broader technology ecosystem. SpaceX operates the Starlink satellite network and provides launch services for commercial customers and government agencies, while xAI develops large language models and related AI systems, including the Grok chatbot. The combined valuation of roughly $1.25 trillion reflects recent private market assessments of both companies, according to the reports. At the same time, xAI’s valuation surged rapidly following funding rounds and its acquisition of the social media platform X. People familiar with the discussions said the merger is designed to simplify ownership and governance ahead of a potential public listing. An IPO at the reported valuation would place the merged entity among the most valuable technology companies globally, rivalling established public market leaders in scale. The merger highlights Musk’s strategy of integrating his businesses to support long-term technological goals. By bringing AI capabilities closer to SpaceX’s satellite and space infrastructure, the company could explore new applications such as AI-powered communications, data processing and autonomous systems. The scale of the proposed merger is likely to attract regulatory attention, particularly given SpaceX’s extensive contracts with US government agencies, including NASA and the Department of Defence. Analysts have also pointed to governance challenges, as Musk holds leadership roles across several major companies. So far, neither SpaceX nor xAI has released detailed public statements outlining governance structures or how operations will be integrated. In 2025, it acquired X, deepening Musk’s push to combine data, distribution and AI development. The merger follows earlier consolidation moves within Musk’s business portfolio aimed at streamlining operations ahead of public market access.

# The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. ## The Crucial Role of Valuation and Funding in AI's Ascent. Understanding how AI companies are valued and how they secure funding rounds is paramount for anyone looking to navigate or participate in this dynamic sector. This post will delve deep into the mechanics of AI funding rounds and the specific factors that influence valuation, offering practical insights into what makes an AI venture truly valuable in the eyes of the market and investors. The journey of an AI startup, much like any tech venture, typically involves a series of funding rounds, each serving a distinct purpose and attracting different types of investors. Valuation here is highly speculative, often based on the strength of the team, the novelty of the AI idea, and the perceived market potential rather than existing revenue or users. ### Series A: Proving Product-Market Fit. Once an AI company has a working MVP and demonstrates initial traction – perhaps with early users or pilot programs – it typically seeks **Series A funding**. For highly successful AI companies, late-stage funding may involve private equity firms or pre-IPO rounds, as they prepare for a potential public offering (IPO) or a major acquisition. ## The Nuances of AI Company Valuation: Beyond Traditional Metrics. AI's disruptive potential often means companies are valued not just on current revenue, but on their ability to capture a massive **Total Addressable Market (TAM)**. While revenue multiples eventually become important, early-stage AI companies might be valued more on user engagement, unique model adoption, or even the sheer computational power and efficiency of their AI. ## Challenges and Future Outlook in AI Valuation and Funding. Understanding **Valuation, Funding** in the AI sector is more than just comprehending financial terms; it's about grasping the intrinsic value of innovation, data, and human ingenuity. Unlike traditional AI systems that primarily analyze data or make predictions based on existing patterns, generative AI models create entirely new, original content.

items.raw_snippet: # Artificial Intelligence on Merger and Acquisition Processes: Observation from The Target Identification and Due Diligence Perspective. The aim of the study is to analyse the impact of AI on mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the areas of target identification and due diligence. Although considerable research based on customary statistical techniques and some contemporary Computational Intelligence techniques have been devoted to identify takeover targets, most of the existing studies are based upon multiple previous mergers and acquisitions. In this paper we are exploring the mergers and acquisitions (M&A) processes and how they are influenced by digitization, as well as highlighting the accompanying risks that digitization brings to this field. From the last few decades, maximum studies focused to understand the importance of going into the deal of Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A). AI in mergers and acquisitions: Insights into the due diligence process. How does AI enhance the due diligence process in mergers and acquisitions? How does AI improve risk management in mergers and acquisitions? The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Enhancing Decision-making and Efficiency in Mergers and Acquisitions: A Case Study Approach within the U.S. Capital Market. This study explores the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in enhancing decision-making and operational efficiency in mergers and acquisitions (M&A) within the U.S. capital market. In recent years, AI technologies have been increasingly adopted to support various stages of the M&A process, including target identification, due diligence, valuation, and integration. Using a mixed-methods approach that combines quantitative analysis of 150 U.S. financial institutions over three years with qualitative case studies of twelve firms adopting AI-driven sourcing platforms, the research examines applications of machine learning algorithms, natural language processing, and predictive analytics in identifying acquisition opportunities. Post-merger integration (PMI) is the process of integrating two or more organizations together in a scope of Merger & Acquisition (M&A) initiative. Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) have long attracted managers’ attention and have been researched in different perspectives and using different theories. Given the high level of uncertainty, time-consuming nature, and inertia of technology exploration/exploitation through internal Research and Development (R&D), the strategic use of mergers and acquisitions (M&A) to obtain new technological knowledge/capabilities has become a common corporate phenomenon.

# SpaceX Merger Talks With xAI Ahead of Planned IPO Launch. SpaceX is in discussions to merge with Elon Musk’s artificial intelligence company xAI as it considers steps ahead of a potential initial public offering expected in 2026. The talks focus on bringing xAI’s AI operations under SpaceX’s corporate structure as the rocket company reviews its long-term strategy. SpaceX and xAI are holding merger discussions, as reported by Reuters, as Elon Musk evaluates restructuring options ahead of a planned IPO. If completed, the transaction would consolidate Musk’s space and artificial intelligence businesses within a single company. SpaceX Chief Financial Officer Bret Johnsen is listed as an officer in both filings, with SpaceX named as a managing member in one entity. The proposed merger is expected to be structured primarily as a share exchange, under which xAI equity would be converted into SpaceX stock. ## IPO Planning and Corporate Structure. SpaceX has been exploring options for a public listing, with 2026 under consideration. Combining xAI with SpaceX could streamline the group’s corporate structure ahead of an IPO and present investors with a business spanning aerospace, satellite communications and artificial intelligence. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in satellite network management, launch operations and data analysis. Integrating xAI could support SpaceX’s efforts to expand AI capabilities internally as competition grows across both the space and technology sectors. SpaceX was valued at about $800 billion in recent private share transactions, while xAI was valued at roughly $230 billion following a funding round in late 2025. A merger could influence SpaceX’s valuation narrative ahead of an IPO, while also adding complexity to its business profile. SpaceX and xAI have not issued public comments on the reported discussions. Elon Musk has also not made a public statement regarding the merger talks. Elon Musk controls several major companies, including SpaceX, xAI, Tesla and Neuralink. In 2025, xAI acquired social media platform X in an all-stock transaction, expanding its access to data used for AI development. SpaceX operates the Starlink satellite internet network and provides launch services to commercial and government customers. xAI develops artificial intelligence models, including the Grok chatbot, and has pursued enterprise and defence-related AI contracts.

# The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. The Business of AI: Understanding Funding Rounds and Valuation in Artificial Intelligence. ## The Crucial Role of Valuation and Funding in AI's Ascent. Understanding how AI companies are valued and how they secure funding rounds is paramount for anyone looking to navigate or participate in this dynamic sector. This post will delve deep into the mechanics of AI funding rounds and the specific factors that influence valuation, offering practical insights into what makes an AI venture truly valuable in the eyes of the market and investors. The journey of an AI startup, much like any tech venture, typically involves a series of funding rounds, each serving a distinct purpose and attracting different types of investors. Valuation here is highly speculative, often based on the strength of the team, the novelty of the AI idea, and the perceived market potential rather than existing revenue or users. ### Series A: Proving Product-Market Fit. Once an AI company has a working MVP and demonstrates initial traction – perhaps with early users or pilot programs – it typically seeks **Series A funding**. For highly successful AI companies, late-stage funding may involve private equity firms or pre-IPO rounds, as they prepare for a potential public offering (IPO) or a major acquisition. ## The Nuances of AI Company Valuation: Beyond Traditional Metrics. While revenue multiples eventually become important, early-stage AI companies might be valued more on user engagement, unique model adoption, or even the sheer computational power and efficiency of their AI. ## Challenges and Future Outlook in AI Valuation and Funding. Understanding **Valuation, Funding** in the AI sector is more than just comprehending financial terms; it's about grasping the intrinsic value of innovation, data, and human ingenuity. items.raw_snippet: # Anthropic teams with Goldman, Blackstone and others on $1.5 billion AI venture targeting PE-owned firms. * Anthropic is partnering with Goldman Sachs, Blackstone and Hellman & Friedman to deploy Claude across their portfolio companies and beyond. * The venture is also backed by a wider group of asset managers including Apollo Global Management and General Atlantic. * The new firm will embed engineers inside mid-sized companies to redesign workflows around agents, targeting a key talent bottleneck in AI. Anthropic said Monday it is partnering with private equity giants Goldman Sachs and Blackstone to launch a $1.5 billion firm aimed at speeding the adoption of artificial intelligence across hundreds of companies. The new entity, formed alongside the San Francisco-based PE firm Hellman & Friedman and backed by a group of asset managers including Apollo and General Atlantic, will deploy Anthropic's Claude AI model directly inside businesses, starting with companies owned by the investment firms.

items.raw_snippet: # Sam Altman expected to testify as OpenAI trial resumes in Oakland. A high-profile trial over artificial intelligence resumes Monday morning in Oakland. A high-profile trial over artificial intelligence resumes Monday morning in Oakland, and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman is expected to take the stand at some point. Elon Musk is suing Altman and OpenAI for $134 billion, claiming the company abandoned its original nonprofit mission and instead shifted toward making a profit — while using his connections and expertise. He told the court the company was originally created as a charity focused on developing AI that is safe and beneficial to humanity, without the pressure to make money. “There have been a lot of claims that a charity was stolen, and we believe and now know that the evidence is going to show that the Open AI Foundation has been in command of Open AI from the beginning and remains in control of the organization,” said William Savitt, an attorney for OpenAI. ### OpenAI trial: Elon Musk returns to the stand.

items.title: BNY CEO says AI is a jobs creator, not a destroyer | American Banker
items.snippet: * **Key insight:** The deployment of AI is a way for companies to create more in...
items.raw_snippet: * **Key insight:** The deployment of AI is a way for companies to create more investment capacity, BNY CEO Robin Vince said Monday during a panel discussion at the Milken Institute's 2026 global conference. * **Expert quote:** "I think when you can save in one place, it allows you to be able to do more." — Vince. In the face of critics who contend that artificial intelligence will kill jobs, the top executive at The Bank of New York Mellon on Monday defended the firm's decision to embrace the technology, arguing that AI allows companies to invest in new jobs and new markets. The adoption of AI, according to BNY CEO Robin Vince, creates capacity for knowledge-based work that will create positive operating leverage for the companies that choose to deploy it. "I don't think it's just words," Vince said at a panel discussion at the Milken Institute's annual conference, referring to his belief that savings from AI will allow companies to make additional investments.
